subject: Post-demo: prewarmed instances, streaming SLO criteria & scale-test next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Susan Patel <susan@atlaspayments.com>, Mike Cho <mike@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap — streaming SLOs, prewarm triggers, and next actions

Hi Susan / Mike —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a proposed plan so we’re aligned on what we need from Atlas to validate production SLOs for your agent-facing product. Key points from today: 

- Target SLOs you called out: 95th percentile token-streaming latency <= 180ms, 99th <= 320ms for sessions with live streaming (token-by-token), and tail latency budget that preserves interactive UX under load.
- Peak concurrency expectation: baseline 350 concurrent streams during business hours; traffic spikes up to 650 concurrent for incident/problem windows (15–45 minutes).
- Acceptable scale-up window: you want 90% of spike capacity reachable within 90 seconds from baseline (warm pool + autoscale), with queueing behavior that maintains percentile SLOs rather than failing fast.
- Preferred degradation model: graceful degradation by switching to a compatible lower-cost model variant and enabling token-throttling, rather than wholesale failures.

Action items we propose: 
1) Share a short SLO matrix (attached) with explicit test thresholds we will run during the scale test.
2) Schedule a scale test in our dedicated sandbox for a 2-hour window (we suggest Tue Dec 6 10:00–12:00 PT).
3) Provide a small sample production-like traffic trace from Atlas (5–15 minutes) that we can replay to seed the test and help calibrate warm pool size.
4) Confirm the acceptable model fallbacks and any data residency constraints for the test.

Jordan (cc’d) will own the technical runbook and will follow up with the exact test plan and what logs/metrics to expect. Neha can advise on the warm-pool sizing heuristics based on your concurrency distribution once we have the replay trace.

Next meeting: propose a 30-min prep call on Thursday to finalize the replay and runbook. Do these times work for you?

Attachments: 20261130-slo-matrix.xlsx, scale-test-runbook.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Susan Patel <susan@atlaspayments.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — streaming SLOs, prewarm triggers, and next actions

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. All items look right. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 650 concurrent number is upper bound for short bursts (we typically see 8–12 min peaks). If you can reach 90% capacity in 90s we’ll consider that acceptable.
- We definitely prefer graceful degradation over error spikes. For fallbacks, our engineering team is okay with switching from your "redwood-stream-v2" model to a smaller "redwood-stream-v1-quant" variant during sustained spikes.
- We can provide a 10-minute trace (redacted) for Monday night — will send via the link you provided.

We’re good to schedule the scale test for Tue Dec 6 10:00–12:00 PT. Can you confirm what observable metrics you’ll provide in real time (e.g., 1s/5s P50/P95/P99, queue length, warm pool utilization, instance spin-up timeline)?

Best,
Susan Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | Atlas Payments
susan@atlaspayments.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Susan Patel <susan@atlaspayments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — streaming SLOs, prewarm triggers, and next actions

Hi Susan — quick technical note on metrics and what we’ll surface during the run: 

We will provide a real-time dashboard with the following streams (published every 5s):
- per-second token emission latency (P50 / P95 / P99) for streaming sessions
- request concurrency (active streams) and queued requests count
- warm-pool size and percent utilization (instances prewarmed and idle vs warm-allocating)
- instance spin-up timeline (timestamped events for cold start -> ready)
- model fallback events (if we promote fallback variant) and resulting average token latency post-fallback

Runbook excerpts: 
- Warm-pool strategy: we’ll provision a conservative warm-pool equal to 40% of your baseline concurrency (so ~140 prewarmed instances for the 350 baseline). During the test we’ll dynamically adjust warm-pool target based on replayed burst shapes.
- Autoscaling behavior: continuous batching plus incremental instance adds; we target first capacity tranche within 25–40s and steady ramp to full target by 90s depending on burst steepness.
- Queueing policy: default FIFO short-queue (target queue depth < 200) with adaptive backpressure if P95 latency exceeds SLO; we’ll record refused-connections as a last resort.

Logs/telemetry: we’ll stream metrics to the dashboard and push raw trace logs to the shared GCS bucket for post-test analysis. Expect an initial telemetry package (baseline metrics + trace) within 24h of the run.

If that matches your expectations we’ll lock the run window and I’ll share the dashboard link and ingestion keys.

-Jordan
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

Thanks all — locking Tue Dec 6 10:00–12:00 PT for the scale test. Final checklist for Atlas (please reply if anything is missing):

- Send the 10-minute redacted traffic trace by EOD Tue Dec 1 (we will confirm receipt).
- Confirm access for a single engineer to the Atlas staging endpoint (read-only replay access) during the run.
- Review & sign the small test agreement (DocuSign) — procurement included on cc.
- Confirm which model variant to use as fallback (Susan suggested redwood-stream-v1-quant).

Deliverables from Redwood during/after the run: 
- Live dashboard with P50/P95/P99 token-stream latency, queue depth, warm-pool utilization, instance spin-up timeline (link and keys inbound by Wed Dec 2).
- Post-test report capturing whether SLOs were met and recommended warm-pool sizing and autoscale tweaks.
- Actionable MAP updates (I’ll record outcomes in the shared MAP doc).

Procurement team — please expect a DocuSign for a short test agreement and a brief cost estimate for the sandbox hours.

If no objections, I’ll send the calendar invite and attach the final runbook in the event.

Thanks — looking forward to the test.
